hypotheses.claim: TEA/TEOA differences arise mainly because the amine changes proton-management and local CO2 environment, not only electron donation; TEOA may favor different proton or CO2-associated states than TEA. A discriminating prediction is that donor-dependent CO/H2 differences track medium or isotope-sensitive observables and can weaken when proton-delivery or solvent/composition variables are tightly normalized.
hypotheses.alternative: The dominant TEA/TEOA effect is intrinsic donor redox chemistry or cobalt-state formation, and matching proton-source or medium variables will not substantially collapse the selectivity difference.
hypotheses.platform_and_comparator_choice: P01 is preferred because the donor substitution can be anchored to one Co-bpy baseline while keeping MeCN/H2O and g-C3N4 constant; TEA and TEOA are treated as multifunctional additives rather than pure reductants. No extra platform is needed unless P01 cannot separate donor identity from medium shifts.
hypotheses.uncertainty: Evidence for CO2 capture, proton relay, or adduct formation is cross-system and often interpretive, so transfer to Co-bpy remains speculative until matched controls are done. TEA and TEOA likely change several coupled properties at once, making full causal separation difficult.

candidates.title: Medium-normalized TEA vs TEOA with attribution controls
candidates.purpose: Test whether the TEA/TEOA CO/H2 difference in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system persists after tighter recipe matching, while embedding internal attribution controls so any collapse of the difference is interpreted only as reduced compatibility with a strong medium-dominant explanation rather than proof of a specific proton-management mechanism.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 directly anchors the CoCl2+bpy/g-C3N4/MeCN:H2O/TEOA platform and notes TEA as a related donor option. EV061, EV013, GX009, and EV031 are transferred only as source observations that amines and solvent environments can alter CO2 association, proton availability, viscosity, conductivity, coordination environment, and intermediate stability. The proposal therefore compares TEA and TEOA within one anchored formulation family, adds no-amine and Ar controls for attribution, and narrows inference because composition normalization cannot make TEA and TEOA chemically equivalent.

comparisons.inference: Descriptive anchored comparison: whether an apparent TEA/TEOA selectivity difference is reproduced in the literature-linked recipe.
Primary bounded comparison: if a difference remains after the defined composition normalization, donor identity or other donor-linked properties still matter within this constrained recipe family.
Normalization-effect check within TEOA; this multi-factor contrast shows whether normalization itself changes output and therefore how strongly the anchored comparison was composition-sensitive.
Normalization-effect check within TEA; large changes indicate that the unnormalized donor comparison was materially confounded by recipe composition.
CO2-attribution control for the normalized TEOA condition; CO observed mainly under CO2 supports assignment of carbon-containing products to the intended feed rather than background contamination.
CO2-attribution control for the normalized TEA condition; H2 may persist under Ar, so this contrast mainly bounds carbon-product attribution rather than hydrogen pathways.
Necessity-oriented comparison for added amine in the normalized TEOA recipe family, but not a single-factor causal test because amine removal also changes total liquid composition logic.
Necessity-oriented comparison for added amine in the normalized TEA recipe family, likewise confounded by composition change and therefore bounded to functional necessity rather than mechanism.

procedure: Select one executable P01 baseline from EV059, then pilot catalyst loading, g-C3N4 amount, reactor fill, and sampling times to obtain quantifiable CO and H2 without detector saturation or immediate deactivation.

Prepare all groups with the same cobalt source, bpy source, g-C3N4 batch, reactor geometry, illumination program, and analytical workflow; for E13G03-E13G06 explicitly match MeCN/H2O and total amine-derived fraction across TEA and TEOA normalized groups.
Run the irradiations under identical timing and temperature control, sampling headspace at common time points for CO and H2 in one calibration campaign that includes the Ar and no-amine groups.
Report CO amount, H2 amount, and CO/H2 time profiles for every group, and record bulk pre- and post-run apparent pH plus visible phase or precipitation changes only as comparability covariates.

Interpret the normalized TEA versus TEOA contrast narrowly, using the control groups to confirm baseline attribution and to avoid reading any selectivity collapse as proof of one specific hidden variable.
measurements: Gas-phase CO amount versus time.
Gas-phase H2 amount versus time.
CO/H2 ratio or selectivity versus time calculated from jointly measured products.
Bulk pre- and post-run apparent pH of the liquid phase as a covariate only.
Qualitative notes on color change, precipitation, or phase separation as comparability checks only.
Analytical blank and calibration stability across the full sample set.
candidates.supports: Supports the medium-dominant version of H03 only in a narrowed sense if a TEA/TEOA difference evident in the anchored recipe becomes substantially smaller or disappears in the normalized comparison, while the CO2 and no-amine controls show that the normalized experiment still produces attributable signal. This would indicate that recipe-linked medium effects contribute materially, without identifying which hidden variable is responsible.
candidates.refutes: Refutes the stronger medium-dominant emphasis of H03 if the TEA/TEOA difference is reproduced with similar direction and magnitude in both anchored and normalized comparisons, suggesting that the controlled composition variables are not the main source of the selectivity difference. That outcome would be more compatible with donor-specific redox, coordination, or cobalt-state alternatives, though not uniquely proving any one of them.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if one or more normalized groups give signal near detection limits, if normalization causes incompatible catalyst stability or phase behavior, if the Ar or no-amine controls reveal strong background artifacts, or if the observed TEA/TEOA differences are comparable to run-to-run analytical uncertainty.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent literature values. Use the EV059-linked recipe family only to choose the starting composition logic, then pilot the minimum necessary executable settings: catalyst loading window, support amount, irradiation time, sampling interval, and gas calibration range. For normalized groups, hold MeCN/H2O ratio and total amine-derived fraction constant across TEA and TEOA where physically feasible; if miscibility or handling prevents exact matching, document the deviation and narrow the inference rather than asserting equivalence.
candidates.limitations: TEA and TEOA remain chemically nonequivalent even after composition normalization, so this card cannot isolate proton activity, dissolved CO2, viscosity, conductivity, and cobalt coordination effects from one another. The no-amine comparison also changes overall liquid composition and therefore tests functional necessity more than pure mechanistic causality. Product data alone cannot identify the active cobalt species or the dominant hidden variable behind any selectivity shift.

candidates.title: Isotope-sensitive operando signatures in TEA vs TEOA Co-bpy photocatalysis
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA give different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic features under matched P01 CO2-reduction conditions, consistent with different proton-management or hydrogen-containing states rather than a donor effect visible only in product ratios.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV080 supports isotope substitution as a transferable assignment aid in operando FTIR-type measurements, but not species identity in this Co-bpy system. GX010 and GX015 support proton-inventory and isotope logic as discriminators of proton-delivery environments in cobalt CO2-reduction chemistry, not as direct evidence for this photocatalyst. EV031 supports the transferable idea that donor/solvent environment can change detectable intermediate populations and selectivity in bipyridine-based CO2 reduction. Proposed transfer: compare matched TEA and TEOA P01 samples with H2O versus D2O in the same spectroscopic configuration, and interpret isotope-sensitive differences only as evidence for differing hydrogen-coupled observables under these conditions.

comparisons.inference: Within TEOA, isotope-dependent shifts or time-course changes identify hydrogen-coupled observables worth tracking, but do not uniquely assign structure or catalytic relevance.
Within TEA, isotope-sensitive features provide the matched comparator for whether TEA accesses similar or different hydrogen-coupled observables.
Under H2O, donor-dependent spectral differences are descriptive only; if absent, a strong proton-management explanation is weakened but not excluded.

Under D2O, persistence or loss of donor-dependent signatures helps bound whether TEA/TEOA differences track hydrogen-coupled observables or remain compatible with cobalt-state and donor-redox alternatives.

procedure: Verify one exact spectroscopic mode before comparison and apply it to all groups; if true operando sensitivity is inadequate in pilot, switch the whole card to a fixed-delay near-operando transfer protocol rather than mixing modes.

Prepare matched P01 TEA and TEOA samples from the same cobalt source, bpy source, g-C3N4 batch, solvent family, cell geometry, and CO2 handling; include donor-free background if signal quality permits.

Run a pilot to set path length, loading, and acquisition window by criteria of unsaturated spectra, manageable scattering/background drift, and repeatable catalyst-region features; reject settings that differ in baseline quality between TEA and TEOA beyond preset tolerance.
Acquire time-resolved spectra for H2O- and D2O-containing TEA and TEOA samples under the same illumination and gas conditions, with matched dark or pre-illumination references for subtraction.
Track reproducible band positions, intensities, and time profiles, and compare them with parallel CO and H2 measurements only as correlation, not mechanism proof.
measurements: Time-resolved operando or fixed-delay near-operando spectra in predefined regions assigned only as candidate hydrogen-coupled, CO2-derived, ligand-associated, or background-sensitive features
Isotope-induced shifts, attenuation, or altered temporal evolution upon H2O to D2O substitution within each donor condition
Difference spectra versus dark, pre-illumination, and donor-free references to identify background or support-derived contributions
Replicate agreement of donor-dependent isotope responses across independently prepared samples
Parallel CO and H2 product amounts from matched runs to test whether spectral differences co-occur with selectivity differences without equating them
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent isotope response under matched acquisition: TEA and TEOA differ in H/D-sensitive band positions, magnitudes, or time behavior beyond donor-free/background changes, and the difference is not explained by obvious baseline artifacts. Stronger but still non-decisive support occurs if donor-dependent catalytic CO/H2 divergence also weakens or reorganizes under the same D2O substitution.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 would be that TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions, while spectra are dominated by shared or non-isotope-sensitive changes. If catalytic TEA/TEOA differences remain substantial in matched runs despite indistinguishable H/D-sensitive signatures, a proton-management-centered account is weakened relative to alternatives.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if signal-to-background is inadequate, scattering from the suspension obscures donor comparisons, assignment remains dominated by overlapping support/solvent features, or D2O substitution changes bulk properties enough that spectral differences cannot be bounded to hydrogen-coupled observables. Donor-dependent but non-isotope-sensitive changes are also inconclusive for H03 because they remain compatible with cobalt speciation or donor photoredox effects.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-anchored P01 formulation family only after verifying exact baseline composition from supplied source records. Calibrate path length, catalyst loading, aqueous fraction, and acquisition interval by pilot criteria of stable baseline, detectable catalyst-region signal, and repeatable spectra across replicate preparations. Predefine acceptable baseline-drift and scattering thresholds before comparing donors. Keep preparation order and nominal component identities matched between H2O and D2O groups. If pH/pD matching is attempted, document one convention and use it consistently without claiming exact equivalence.
candidates.limitations: This characterization card narrows inference to whether TEA and TEOA differ in isotope-sensitive observables under matched conditions. It cannot uniquely identify intermediates, prove rate-determining roles, or isolate proton management from all other donor-dependent medium changes. D2O perturbs more than proton mass, and TEA versus TEOA also changes donor structure and solution properties. Near-operando measurements may miss the true operating state.

candidates.title: CO2-associated donor speciation under matched P01 medium
candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA and TEOA create different detectable CO2-associated solution states in the P01 medium before illumination or after reaction-relevant equilibration, as a bounded indicator of donor-dependent local CO2/proton environment.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV029 and EV061 motivate checking whether TEOA can participate in CO2-associated adduct or ion-pair chemistry beyond electron donation. GX009 adds transferable concern that cobalt-bipyridine media can change with solvent coordination, water, viscosity, and conductivity. EV031 supports the broader idea that donor/solvent environment can alter observable intermediates and selectivity. Proposed transfer: in matched P01 solvent composition, compare TEA and TEOA by descriptive solution-state spectroscopy. This proposal does not assume the same adduct identity reported in other systems, and any observed bands or shifts would indicate association only, not the catalytic active state or causal mechanism by themselves.

comparisons.inference: Within TEA-containing medium, identifies CO2-induced spectral changes above the inert reference.
Within TEOA-containing medium, identifies CO2-induced spectral changes above the inert reference.
Tests whether TEA and TEOA differ in CO2-associated signatures under otherwise matched medium.

Tests whether any TEOA-specific CO2-associated signal exceeds the no-amine background; this is descriptive and does not isolate whether the signal comes from donor-CO2 association, donor-cobalt coordination, or both.

procedure: Prepare matched P01 media using the same cobalt source, bpy, g-C3N4 loading state, and solvent composition for all groups; equilibrate under inert gas or CO2 in the dark for a fixed pilot-validated time.
Acquire background spectra for solvent-only and component-minus-one references needed to subtract dominant solvent, support, and baseline cobalt-bpy features before assigning donor-dependent changes.
Measure each group by one primary solution-state method suitable for CO2-associated bands or shifts, with an orthogonal confirmatory method if pilot signal quality is sufficient.
If a CO2-dependent donor-specific feature appears, repeat on independently prepared samples and check reversibility by switching gas condition or brief degassing where chemically safe.
Record sample appearance, pH or apparent acidity metric where feasible, and conductivity or other simple covariates so spectral differences are not interpreted without medium-context notes.
measurements: Difference IR spectra of CO2-equilibrated minus inert-equilibrated samples, tracking new or shifted bands attributable to donor- or bicarbonate/carbonate-associated environments.
NMR chemical-shift or line-shape changes for donor-containing samples before and after CO2 equilibration, if the medium permits interpretable spectra.
Background-reference spectra for no-amine and component-minus-one samples to bound non-donor contributions.
Simple covariates such as apparent acidity metric and conductivity; these can contextualize medium changes but cannot establish molecular identity on their own.
Replicate consistency of any donor-specific CO2-responsive signal; reproducibility is required before using the signal in later catalytic correlation studies.
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference in CO2-responsive spectral features under matched P01 medium, especially if TEOA and TEA show distinct changes relative to their own inert references and the no-amine background. This would support a local CO2/proton-environment contribution, while remaining associational until linked to catalytic outcomes under the same controls.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03-dominant interpretation would be no reproducible donor-specific CO2-responsive difference despite adequate detection sensitivity and clean backgrounds, especially if TEA and TEOA appear spectroscopically similar under matched medium. That would weaken the case that donor-linked CO2-associated speciation is a main explanation, though it would not prove a redox-only mechanism.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if spectra are dominated by solvent/support overlap, if signals are near detection limits, if assignments depend on a single ambiguous band, or if donor substitution also changes uncontrolled covariates enough that the contrast becomes multi-factor in practice. Observing a new signal without assignment controls cannot establish adduct identity or catalytic relevance.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent fixed acquisition settings. Pilot first to choose sample concentration, path length, equilibration time, and whether IR, NMR, or both have usable signal-to-background in the actual P01 medium. Set the lowest concentration that still gives reproducible donor and CO2-responsive features without obvious precipitation or severe scattering from g-C3N4. Use the same preparation order, gas-contact protocol, and delay before measurement across groups. If g-C3N4 prevents interpretable solution-state spectra, run a matched clarified-supernatant variant as a bounded adaptation and label the transfer limitation explicitly rather than claiming fully equivalent operating chemistry.
candidates.limitations: This characterization is descriptive. A donor-specific CO2-responsive signal cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate, the active cobalt state, or the cause of CO/H2 selectivity. g-C3N4 and cobalt-bpy may contribute overlapping features, and dark-equilibrated samples may miss illumination-generated states. If donor identity changes pH, coordination, or suspension properties simultaneously, the comparison remains mechanistically mixed even when composition is nominally matched.

candidates.title: Amine omission and bounded inert-base replacement
candidates.purpose: Test whether amine presence is necessary in the P01 TEA/TEOA comparison and whether a tightly screened non-donor base can shift outcomes in a limited way consistent with mixed proton-management contributions, without claiming replacement of sacrificial donation.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV013 supports treating TEA and TEOA as multifunctional additives that can act as H+ source and hole scavenger, so omission is needed before interpreting identity effects. EV024, GX010, and GX015 support the narrower proposition that proton-delivery environment can alter CO2-reduction behavior, motivating a bounded non-donor base screen. GX008 supports matched negative controls and broad product analysis. Transfer is limited because no supplied evidence shows a non-sacrificial base reproducing the target Co-bpy photocatalysis; any rescue is therefore descriptive evidence for partial proton-management contribution only.

candidates.supports: H03 is supported if amine omission strongly suppresses or shifts the baseline behavior and the pre-screened non-donor base causes a reproducible partial movement in total activity or CO/H2 distribution toward the TEOA case, while TEA and TEOA still differ under matched conditions.
candidates.refutes: H03 is weakened if the non-donor base produces no reproducible shift relative to no amine and TEA versus TEOA differences remain large under otherwise matched conditions, especially if omission mainly removes activity in a way consistent with loss of donor function alone.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if the selected base causes new background reactivity, instability, or phase changes; if acid-base conditions cannot be compared meaningfully; or if product signals are near detection limits.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations. Use the verified P01 baseline for TEA and TEOA conditions. For the replacement arm, first screen candidate non-donor bases in the same solvent matrix and choose one condition only if it meets all pilot criteria: negligible CO and H2 in catalyst-free or no-light blanks, no obvious decomposition or precipitation before irradiation, and a measurable change in a bulk acid-base descriptor relative to E16G02. If no candidate meets these criteria, retain only E16G01/E16G02/E16G04 and report the replacement arm as blocked.
candidates.limitations: The replacement arm remains limited because a non-donor base cannot reproduce sacrificial electron donation. Positive rescue can also reflect ionic-strength, coordination, viscosity, or solvation changes. Negative rescue cannot exclude proton-management contributions. Bulk acid-base descriptors in MeCN/H2O may not represent local proton delivery. This card therefore tests necessity and bounded medium sensitivity, not full causal separation.

candidates.source_to_proposal: Source observations are cross-system: TEOA proportion and water/solvent environment can alter CO2 reduction output and intermediate visibility, and TEA/TEOA can function as proton-source/hole-scavenging co-solvents. This proposal does not assume the same intermediates or mechanisms are present in Co-bpy/g-C3N4; it tests whether the donor effect collapses or crosses over under tighter medium control.

Compare donor differences within each water setting and water-setting effects within each donor; if a strong donor difference is seen at one setting but collapses or reverses at the other, flag this as medium-dependent rather than donor-identity-only behavior.
measurements: CO amount or formation rate by gas analysis
H2 amount or formation rate by gas analysis
CO/H2 selectivity ratio or fraction with uncertainty across replicates
Total detectable gaseous products covered by the chosen workflow, to avoid selective reporting
Apparent medium descriptor before and after reaction: pH or pD if interpretable in the mixed medium, otherwise conductivity as a bounded proxy
Qualitative phase behavior or precipitation check, because medium change can alter accessibility without proving mechanism
candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a clear donor-by-water interaction: TEA and TEOA differ strongly at one MeCN/H2O setting but the difference narrows, disappears, or crosses over at the other, with accompanying shifts in medium descriptors. That pattern would indicate that the donor effect is substantially mediated by proton-management or local medium/CO2 environment rather than being fixed by donor identity alone.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 would be that TEA and TEOA show a similar directional CO/H2 difference of comparable magnitude at both water settings while each donor is otherwise stable and analytically well matched. That would favor an explanation dominated by donor-specific redox or cobalt-state effects that are not substantially collapsed by this medium normalization.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include very low product formation, unstable phase behavior, unequal catalyst suspension or light absorption across water settings, analytical uncertainty larger than the donor effect, or simultaneous large changes in conductivity/dispersion that prevent attributing differences specifically to proton-management versus other medium changes.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent solvent fractions. Choose two water settings by pilot within the literature-supported MeCN/H2O family: one near the current baseline and one more water-rich, but only if both remain operationally comparable for TEA and TEOA. Hold total solvent volume constant. Keep the same nominal donor condition for TEA and TEOA as an initial comparator, then verify by pilot that neither donor causes immediate deactivation, phase separation, or complete quenching failure. If apparent pH is not reliable in the mixed solvent, record it only as a bounded descriptor and prioritize conductivity and product outputs.
candidates.limitations: This card cannot isolate a unique cause because changing water fraction also changes viscosity, conductivity, CO2 solubility, donor protonation, and catalyst/support environment. Even single-factor pairwise contrasts are embedded in a system where effective photon absorption and cobalt speciation may shift with medium. A crossover is therefore strong descriptive evidence for medium involvement but not proof of a specific proton-relay or CO2-adduct mechanism. No claim of matched chemistry should be made from generic donor labels alone.

candidates.purpose: Test whether TEA versus TEOA differences in the P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 system reproducibly co-vary with directly measured bulk proton-management and medium descriptors, while keeping the conclusion descriptive rather than causal.
candidates.source_to_proposal: The sources support treating TEA and TEOA as multifunctional additives that can alter proton supply, CO2-associated solution behavior, conductivity, viscosity, and related medium properties, and they show that isotope-sensitive proton-transfer tests can be mechanistically informative in other cobalt systems. The proposal transfers only the need to measure donor-dependent covariates alongside catalytic outputs within one fixed baseline formulation. It does not assume that bulk descriptors equal the local environment at cobalt or g-C3N4, and it excludes the previously overreaching CO2-uptake proxy as a core readout.

Within TEOA, isotope-sensitive changes test whether product distribution and measured bulk descriptors respond to a proton-related perturbation, while recognizing that solvent isotope substitution changes multiple properties.
Within TEA, the corresponding isotope comparison asks whether proton-related perturbation measurably alters products or descriptors in the alternative donor environment.

TEOA versus TEA under the same isotope condition tests whether the donor contrast persists after a matched isotope perturbation; persistence weakens a simple bulk proton-management-only account, while collapse supports that account only descriptively.

procedure: Prepare the four matched formulations from one verified P01 stock plan, changing only amine identity and water isotope while keeping reactor geometry, gas handling, illumination, and sampling times identical.

After the same CO2 equilibration routine for each sample, measure only bulk descriptors that pass an initial stability pilot in the actual reaction medium, prioritizing one calibrated acidity proxy and conductivity before irradiation.

candidates.supports: Support for H03 would be a reproducible association in which TEA and TEOA show different CO/H2 behavior together with different stable bulk descriptor values or shifts, and the matched D2O perturbation alters the donor contrast in a way consistent across repeats. This supports a contribution from medium or proton-management differences, not a complete mechanism.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H03 as the main explanation would be that TEA and TEOA give reproducibly different CO/H2 outputs while the validated bulk descriptors remain indistinguishable within uncertainty and the isotope perturbation does not materially change the donor contrast. That would shift attention toward explanations such as donor-dependent quenching or cobalt-state formation.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if catalytic differences are not reproducible, if acidity or conductivity measurements are unstable in the mixed suspension, if isotope substitution causes uncontrolled formulation changes, or if descriptor differences appear without any consistent relation to product behavior across matched repeats. Bulk correlation cannot establish local interfacial conditions or specific intermediates.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-anchored P01 formulation only as the starting recipe and verify any missing numerical settings from the supplied source set before execution. First run a pilot in the actual reaction medium to choose one acidity-proxy method that is stable, calibrated, and minimally perturbing; use that single method for every group rather than mixing pH and pD scales. In the same pilot, confirm that conductivity readings are repeatable in catalyst-containing suspensions and define a fixed sampling delay after CO2 equilibration and after irradiation. If D2O materially changes miscibility, suspension stability, or instrument response, keep the H2O donor comparison as the primary test and report isotope arms as bounded descriptive comparisons only.
candidates.limitations: This card is intentionally narrowed to a descriptive covariate screen. TEA and TEOA may simultaneously alter proton transfer, reductive quenching, coordination, viscosity, and CO2 solvation. Bulk acidity and conductivity do not establish the local environment at active sites, and D2O is not a single-factor perturbation. Therefore the experiment can prioritize which explanations deserve stronger follow-up, but it cannot by itself prove proton-management causation.

major_issues: The normalized comparison still leaves major uncontrolled donor-linked properties entangled because matching MeCN/H2O and total amine-derived fraction does not match proton activity, CO2 uptake/speciation, viscosity, conductivity, or cobalt coordination between TEA and TEOA.

The card lacks an internal no-amine or non-CO2 control within the specified groups, so apparent donor-dependent gas differences rely on external workflow checks rather than built-in attribution controls.

The stated inference can overread collapse of the TEA/TEOA difference as mainly medium/proton-management causation, when normalization itself changes several hidden variables and may differentially affect catalyst viability.
decisions.rationale: This is a useful within-platform comparison anchored by direct system evidence for the P01 formulation family and by transferable evidence that amines and medium can alter CO2-reduction behavior. It has clear value as a descriptive test of whether a TEA/TEOA difference survives tighter recipe matching. However, the proposed primary contrast does not isolate donor identity versus medium effects as strongly as claimed, because TEA and TEOA remain chemically non-equivalent even at matched volume fraction and solvent ratio. The design is therefore defensible for researcher consideration only after tightening the interpretation and, ideally, adding explicit attribution controls or covariates that better document what normalization changed.
decisions.prior_issue_resolution: No prior review provided. Current assessment explicitly recognizes the direct P01 anchoring from EV059 while preserving transfer limits from medium-effect evidence. New concerns are the residual confounding after composition normalization, absence of built-in attribution controls in the core group set, and overinterpretation risk if any selectivity collapse is treated as specifically proton-management driven.

major_issues: Signal assignment remains substantially ambiguous because isotope-sensitive bands in this mixed photocatalytic suspension do not uniquely identify donor-specific proton-management states versus cobalt speciation, solvent, or support-related features.
D2O substitution perturbs multiple properties beyond proton transfer, so donor-to-donor isotope differences are not a clean discriminator of proton-management alone.
The operando or near-operando spectroscopy mode is underspecified, making feasibility, background subtraction, and comparability across TEA/TEOA conditions uncertain.
decisions.rationale: The candidate is scientifically valuable as a characterization-heavy discriminator and is supported by transferable method evidence for isotope-assisted operando assignment and by cross-system precedent that solvent/additive environment can alter observed intermediates. The proposed controls are better than many alternatives, including donor-free background and within-donor H2O/D2O contrasts. Still, the card should be revised because the inferential claims need stronger limits and the measurement plan needs more explicit handling of weak signals, scattering, and assignment ambiguity in a g-C3N4-containing photocatalytic mixture. It is worth retaining as a specialist pilot, not as a ready mechanistic test.
decisions.prior_issue_resolution: No prior review provided. Current assessment credits the candidate for including isotope and background controls, but newly flags unresolved assignment ambiguity, solvent-isotope confounding, and missing detail on the exact spectroscopic implementation needed for interpretable comparison.

decisions.rationale: This is a bounded descriptive characterization study with appropriate limits. It does not overclaim mechanistic proof, uses matched inert versus CO2 equilibrated comparisons within each donor, and includes a no-amine background to bound non-donor contributions. The evidence is mostly transferable rather than direct, but it is sufficient for a defensible researcher-facing screen asking whether TEA and TEOA generate different detectable CO2-associated states in the actual P01 medium family. Because the card explicitly treats any signal as associational rather than proof of the active state, the inference is appropriately constrained.
decisions.prior_issue_resolution: No prior review provided. Current assessment notes that the card already resolves common prior-style concerns by adding inert references, no-amine background, reproducibility checks, and explicit warnings against assigning active-species identity from descriptive spectra.

major_issues: The 'non-sacrificial proton-management adjustment or inert base' is too loosely defined, creating major interpretive risk because different replacements could alter coordination, ionic strength, or side reactivity rather than only bulk acid-base environment.
The key rescue comparison is intrinsically confounded: failure to rescue cannot rule out proton-management contributions, while apparent rescue may arise from unrelated medium effects.
The TEA versus inert-adjustment contrast changes more than one factor and cannot support mechanistic ranking unless interpretation is sharply limited.
decisions.rationale: This candidate has practical value because omission and bounded replacement tests can show whether amine presence is necessary and whether some behavior can be moved by a non-donor acid-base intervention. The direct TEA/TEOA comparator also keeps the platform fixed. However, the replacement arm is too open-ended to support the stated mechanistic emphasis without revision. The card should be retained but reframed as a limited intervention screen, with stricter criteria for choosing the replacement and more cautious interpretation of any partial rescue.
decisions.prior_issue_resolution: No prior review provided. Current assessment accepts the card's own limitation that non-sacrificial base cannot replicate donor redox, but identifies unresolved issues in the undefined replacement chemistry and in overreading rescue/failure outcomes beyond what the design can support.

decisions.rationale: This is a defensible descriptive interaction map. It directly addresses the hypothesis prediction that donor-dependent CO/H2 differences may weaken or cross over when medium variables are changed in a controlled way. The card appropriately limits inference to donor-by-medium interaction rather than claiming isolation of a unique mechanism, and it includes practical comparability checks for phase behavior and common analytics. Although evidence is mostly transferable and not direct TEA-versus-TEOA proof in P01, the design is well matched to the stated question and valuable for researcher planning.
decisions.prior_issue_resolution: No prior review provided. Current assessment finds that the card already addresses likely concerns by explicitly treating water-fraction effects as medium-sensitive descriptive evidence, not single-cause mechanism proof, and by requiring an operationally comparable single-phase window for both donors.

major_issues: Bulk descriptors such as pH/pD proxy, conductivity, and CO2 uptake proxy may not track the local environment at cobalt or g-C3N4 sites, so correlation with CO/H2 can be weak or misleading.
The proposal risks overinterpreting paired donor/product/descriptor differences as evidence for proton-management causation when all measured variables can co-vary with other donor-specific effects.
The CO2 uptake-related readout is reactor- and method-dependent and may be difficult to compare cleanly across catalytic suspensions without disturbing the system.
decisions.rationale: The candidate is useful as a low-cost correlation screen and appropriately states that bulk measurements do not prove local mechanism. It gains value from combining catalytic outputs with matched descriptor measurements and isotope perturbation. However, the core inference still needs revision because the measured covariates are indirect, and the suggested uptake proxy may be too method-sensitive for strong conclusions. As a descriptive screen it is worth retaining, but the interpretation should be narrowed and the descriptor suite prioritized toward the most stable, reproducible measures.
decisions.prior_issue_resolution: No prior review provided. Current assessment acknowledges the card's own cautions about bulk-versus-local mismatch, but newly identifies the uptake proxy and correlation-to-causation leap as unresolved issues requiring revision.

previous_review.overall: E15 and E17 are the strongest candidates for shortlist because they ask bounded questions with interpretations that remain aligned to the actual controls. E13, E14, E16, and E18 should be retained in revised form rather than rejected: each has research value, but each currently risks overinterpreting descriptive or confounded contrasts as stronger mechanistic discrimination than the supplied design can support. Across the set, direct support is strongest only for staying within the P01 formulation family; most mechanistic justification is transferable with clear limits. The best near-term package is a low-cost descriptive interaction/characterization sequence: E17 and E15 first, then revised E13 or E18 for follow-up, with E14 reserved for specialist pilot work if simpler screens indicate a real donor-dependent medium effect worth probing spectroscopically.
